glossary.Malignant: Cancerous: able to invade nearby tissue and spread.
glossary.Testis: The male gonad that makes sperm and testosterone; plural testes.
glossary.Undescended testis: A testis that has not moved down into the scrotum by birth or infancy.
glossary.Infertility: Inability to conceive after a year of regular unprotected sex.
glossary.Craggy: Rough and irregular to feel, typical of cancer.
glossary.Scrotum: The skin sac holding the testes.
glossary.Oestrogen: Female sex hormone; a relative excess in men causes breast tissue growth.
glossary.Androgen: Male sex hormone such as testosterone.
glossary.Radiotherapy: Treatment that uses ionising radiation to kill cancer cells.
glossary.Chemotherapy: Drug treatment that kills rapidly dividing cancer cells.
glossary.Prognosis: The likely course and outcome of a disease.
glossary.Metastasise: To spread from the original site to form secondary tumours elsewhere.
glossary.Metastasis: Spread of cancer to a distant site.
glossary.Lymph nodes: Small immune glands that filter lymph; cancer often spreads to them first.
glossary.Spinal cord compression: Pressure on the spinal cord, here from metastases, causing weakness and needing emergency treatment.
glossary.Renal vein: The vein draining blood from the kidney into the inferior vena cava.
glossary.Aorta: The main artery leaving the heart, running down the back of the abdomen.
glossary.Renal cancer: Cancer of the kidney, which can block the left renal vein and cause a varicocele.
glossary.Irreducible: Cannot be pushed back or made smaller.
glossary.Fluctuant: Feels fluid-filled, with a wave of movement when pressed.
glossary.Benign: Not cancerous; does not invade or spread.
glossary.Histology: Examining tissue under a microscope to make the diagnosis.
glossary.Tumour markers: Substances in the blood, such as AFP and hCG, made by some cancers.
glossary.Tumour burden: The total amount of cancer in the body.
glossary.Staging: Working out how far a cancer has spread.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: a cross-sectional X-ray scan.
glossary.Urological: Relating to the urinary tract and male genital organs.
glossary.Etoposide: A chemotherapy drug that blocks the enzyme topoisomerase II; part of BEP.
glossary.Surveillance: Regular check-ups with tests and scans to detect any return of cancer.
glossary.Malignant transformation: The change of normal cells into cancer cells.
glossary.Germ cell: A cell that develops into sperm or eggs.
glossary.Primordial germ cells: The earliest precursor cells that later become sperm or eggs.
glossary.Heterogeneous: Made up of many different types of tissue.
glossary.Differentiated: How closely cells resemble their normal mature form; poorly differentiated cancers are more aggressive.
